extracted.intended_audience: poets, playwrights, literary students, and educated readers of drama
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for dramatic and poetic excellence: characterization, the treatment of universal truths in individual form, moral effect, comedy vs tragedy, and avoidance of sentimentalism or mere spectacle. Focused on how playwrights/poets should shape language, situation, and character to achieve instructive and elevated art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gentlemanly character (portrayal)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The gentlemanly character arises out of the feeling of equality acting as a habit, yet flexible to the varieties of rank, and modified without being disturbed or superseded by them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show gentlemanliness through the whole detail of manners and deportment, in trivial as well as important acts; habitual respect to others that implies an assured anticipation of reciprocal respect. Characterization should present this quality subtly via behavior rather than explicit moralizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drama should not pander to mere laughter or applause
rubrics_metrics.description: "They neither sought in comedy to make us laugh merely, much less to make us laugh by way faces, accidents of jargon, slang phrases for the day... nor did they court tragedy to wheedle away the applause of the spectators..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid writing for transient amusement or applause via topical jokes, cheap faces, or catchphrases. Aim for humor and pathos that arise from human truth and craft, not from ephemeral gags or pandering to popular tastes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragedy should elevate mind and imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: "Their tragic scenes were meant to affect us indeed, but within the bounds of pleasure, and in union with the activity both of our understanding and imagination. They wished to transport the mind to a sense of its possible greatness, and to implant the germs of that greatness..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tragedy ought to inspire and expand the audience's understanding and imagination rather than merely moving them to tears; it should suspend ordinary preoccupations and suggest higher possibilities of character and fate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularize class-characteristics into individual individuality
rubrics_metrics.description: "These class-characteristics, which constitute the instructiveness of a character, are so modified and particularised in each person of the Shakespearian drama, that life itself does not excite more distinctly that sense of individuality..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recognizable class-types or general traits as a foundation, but particularize them into vivid individual characters; balance universal recognizability with distinct, concrete particulars so characters feel both typical and unique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry/drama should clothe the universal in the individual (involution)
rubrics_metrics.description: "One of the essential properties of geometry is not less essential to dramatic excellence... in geometry it is the universal truth itself which is uppermost in the consciousness, in poetry the individual form in which the Truth is clothed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express universal truths through distinctive individual forms and situations. The work's power lies in embodying abstract truths in concrete language, scene, and person, not in abstract exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sentimentalism that flatters without moral sacrifice
rubrics_metrics.description: "Modern sentimental plays filled with the best Christian morality? — just that part of it which you can exercise without a single Christian virtue — without a single sacrifice that is really painful to you."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware moralizing that comforts the audience and affirms their self-regard without requiring genuine ethical cost or transformation. Authentic moral drama should demand real sacrifice or challenge, not provide consolatory flattering sentiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reward criminals or subvert natural moral order for sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: "The whole secret of dramatic popularity consists... in rewarding with the sympathies... those criminals whom law, reason, and religion, have excommunicated from our esteem!"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid plots that invert moral consequences merely to elicit sympathy; do not systematically subvert the natural order of cause and effect in a way that condones vice or makes immorality the path to approbation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic interest arises from manner, language, situation, and passion, not only plot
rubrics_metrics.description: (Dialogue) "Not for the manner? not for the delightful language of the poet? not for the situations, the action and reaction of the passions?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate language, the quality of situations, and the dynamic interplay of passions and reactions; recognize that plot alone (knowing how it ends) does not eliminate dramatic interest if manner and emotional/linguistic craft are strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reuse of familiar plots is acceptable if transformed by treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: "All the stories... pre-existed in the chronicles, ballads, or translations..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality can reside in the handling, language, characterization, and embodiment of themes rather than solely in novel plots. Familiar material is defensible when the poet/playwright renovates it in form and insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy should instruct by revealing natural human growths, reconciling laughter with tenderness
rubrics_metrics.description: "The qualities which these writers portray are ludicrous indeed... yet are they the natural growth of the human mind... and thus prevents... merriment... from degenerating into the heart-poison of contempt or hatred."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make comedy spring from recognisable human traits so laughter leads to understanding and compassion; avoid derisive caricature that inspires contempt rather than reconciliation or insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragic effect must engage understanding as well as feeling (bounded effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Their tragic scenes were meant to affect us... within the bounds of pleasure, and in union with the activity both of our understanding and imagination."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance emotional impact with intellectual engagement; scenes should move the audience but also stimulate reflection and imaginative apprehension of moral/ethical complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid substituting stage spectacle for genuine dramatic substance
rubrics_metrics.description: Anecdote: a deafening explosion and real gunpowder produced astonishment — "the naturalness of the scene was quite astonishing!"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special effects and sensational stage tricks may astonish, but should not replace craft in language, character, and situation. Use spectacle sparingly and ensure it serves deeper artistic and moral aims rather than obscuring weak writing.
